raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-MEX-SustainableValueChains",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Mexican SMEs failing to adopt sustainability criteria face potential forward-exclusion from anchor company global and regional value chains.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Provide dedicated long-term green loans, SLLs, and technical assistance to help SMEs meet anchor company ESG and disclosure standards.",
      "evidence": "Firms that do not comply risk forward-exclusion from supply chains, with implications for sales and employment"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Risk of greenwashing in Sustainability-Linked Sub-loans if sustainability targets and indicators are insufficiently rigorous or unverified.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Mandate ex-ante validation and ex-post verification of Sustainability Plans, KPIs, and targets by qualified independent validation entities.",
      "evidence": "To mitigate the risk of greenwashing, targets and results in the SP will be subject to, respectively, ex-ante validation and ex-post verification"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Low market uptake and limited firm demand for sustainable financing instruments due to high transaction and certification costs.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Deploy Component 2 technical assistance to minimize transaction costs, support project preparation, and partner with anchor companies for outreach.",
      "evidence": "mitigate the risk of a situation where financing is available, but uptake is limited."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Participating financial institutions and firms lack technical capacity to appraise green investments and manage complex MRV requirements.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Deliver technical assistance, standardized templates, digital monitoring tools, and training to PFIs and firms under Component 2.",
      "evidence": "Key constraints go beyond tenor to include high Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) costs and limited capacity to structure, appraise and monitor investments."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Credit risk and borrower default on direct first-tier sub-loans and second-tier PFI on-lending exposures.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Enforce strict eligibility criteria, single-borrower exposure caps, credit risk margins, minimum co-financing, and standard NAFIN credit due diligence.",
      "evidence": "NAFIN will assume the credit risk of the BEs when lending directly and of the PFIs on second-tier operations"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Extreme climate events and hydro-meteorological hazards causing operational disruptions and loan delinquencies for SME/mid-cap borrowers.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Prioritize sub-projects that enhance operational climate resilience, water efficiency, and clean backup energy solutions.",
      "evidence": "Extreme temperatures have been shown to raise loan delinquency rates among Mexican firms, as liquidity shortages and limited access to credit make it difficult"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Foreign exchange rate volatility affecting balance sheet exposures or unhedged sub-borrowers.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Manage balance sheet FX risk using domestic currency swaps and restrict USD-denominated sub-loans to firms with clear natural export hedges.",
      "evidence": "NAFIN will manage the FX risk on its own balance sheet using Mexico’s well developed currency swap market."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Persistent structural gender gaps in financial access limiting women-led businesses from accessing project-supported loan instruments.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish transparent access criteria, gender-focused communication campaigns, and dedicated intermediate results tracking for women-inclusive enterprises.",
      "evidence": "Mexico has a 14 percent gender gap in financial access... women-led businesses face persistent barriers to financing"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Procurement implementation delays arising from NAFIN staff's lack of direct experience conducting World Bank selection processes.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Assign a dedicated qualified procurement professional to the project and provide hands-on training and close supervision from World Bank procurement specialists.",
      "evidence": "while NAFIN staff are familiar with the World Bank Procurement Regulations, they have not been directly involved in carrying out selection and contracting processes."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Financial management efficiency constraints and reporting delays due to reliance on legacy IT systems requiring manual data consolidation.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 2,
      "mitigation": "Establish formal reconciliation procedures, supervisory review workflows, targeted internal audit coverage, and explicit POM financial reporting protocols.",
      "evidence": "efficiency constraints arising from reliance on legacy information systems requiring manual consolidation"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Substantial Environmental and Social (E&S) risks associated with financial intermediary sub-loan portfolios.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Apply NAFIN's ESMS and PFI due diligence, enforce a ring-fenced Exclusion List, and conduct periodic World Bank sample audits of sub-projects.",
      "evidence": "Environmental and Social Risk Classification Substantial"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "High industrial fossil fuel dependence and energy intensity exposing target enterprises to transition risks and energy price spikes.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Target sub-loan allocations to energy efficiency, renewable energy scale-up, and decarbonization investments aligned with Mexico's Sustainable Taxonomy.",
      "evidence": "This combination of fossil fuels and energy intensity means that firms are exposed to both energy-transition risks and high energy costs."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Implementation friction and delay due to novel market application of Sustainability-Linked Loans in the Mexican financial system.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Upgrade NAFIN's Sustainable Finance Framework, pilot SLLs in first-tier operations before scaling to second-tier PFIs, and provide extensive capacity building.",
      "evidence": "While the Project represents the first systematic application of Sustainability Linked Loan (SLL) and Green Loan (GL) debt instruments in Mexico's financial system"
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Mexican SMEs failing to adopt sustainability criteria face potential forward-exclusion from anchor company global and regional value chains.
risks.mitigation: Provide dedicated long-term green loans, SLLs, and technical assistance to help SMEs meet anchor company ESG and disclosure standards.
risks.evidence: Firms that do not comply risk forward-exclusion from supply chains, with implications for sales and employment

risks.description: Risk of greenwashing in Sustainability-Linked Sub-loans if sustainability targets and indicators are insufficiently rigorous or unverified.
risks.mitigation: Mandate ex-ante validation and ex-post verification of Sustainability Plans, KPIs, and targets by qualified independent validation entities.
risks.evidence: To mitigate the risk of greenwashing, targets and results in the SP will be subject to, respectively, ex-ante validation and ex-post verification

risks.description: Low market uptake and limited firm demand for sustainable financing instruments due to high transaction and certification costs.
risks.mitigation: Deploy Component 2 technical assistance to minimize transaction costs, support project preparation, and partner with anchor companies for outreach.
risks.evidence: mitigate the risk of a situation where financing is available, but uptake is limited.

risks.description: Participating financial institutions and firms lack technical capacity to appraise green investments and manage complex MRV requirements.
risks.mitigation: Deliver technical assistance, standardized templates, digital monitoring tools, and training to PFIs and firms under Component 2.
risks.evidence: Key constraints go beyond tenor to include high Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) costs and limited capacity to structure, appraise and monitor investments.

risks.description: Credit risk and borrower default on direct first-tier sub-loans and second-tier PFI on-lending exposures.
risks.mitigation: Enforce strict eligibility criteria, single-borrower exposure caps, credit risk margins, minimum co-financing, and standard NAFIN credit due diligence.
risks.evidence: NAFIN will assume the credit risk of the BEs when lending directly and of the PFIs on second-tier operations

risks.description: Extreme climate events and hydro-meteorological hazards causing operational disruptions and loan delinquencies for SME/mid-cap borrowers.
risks.mitigation: Prioritize sub-projects that enhance operational climate resilience, water efficiency, and clean backup energy solutions.
risks.evidence: Extreme temperatures have been shown to raise loan delinquency rates among Mexican firms, as liquidity shortages and limited access to credit make it difficult

risks.description: Foreign exchange rate volatility affecting balance sheet exposures or unhedged sub-borrowers.
risks.mitigation: Manage balance sheet FX risk using domestic currency swaps and restrict USD-denominated sub-loans to firms with clear natural export hedges.
risks.evidence: NAFIN will manage the FX risk on its own balance sheet using Mexico’s well developed currency swap market.

risks.description: Persistent structural gender gaps in financial access limiting women-led businesses from accessing project-supported loan instruments.
risks.mitigation: Establish transparent access criteria, gender-focused communication campaigns, and dedicated intermediate results tracking for women-inclusive enterprises.
risks.evidence: Mexico has a 14 percent gender gap in financial access... women-led businesses face persistent barriers to financing

risks.description: Procurement implementation delays arising from NAFIN staff's lack of direct experience conducting World Bank selection processes.
risks.mitigation: Assign a dedicated qualified procurement professional to the project and provide hands-on training and close supervision from World Bank procurement specialists.
risks.evidence: while NAFIN staff are familiar with the World Bank Procurement Regulations, they have not been directly involved in carrying out selection and contracting processes.

risks.description: Financial management efficiency constraints and reporting delays due to reliance on legacy IT systems requiring manual data consolidation.
risks.mitigation: Establish formal reconciliation procedures, supervisory review workflows, targeted internal audit coverage, and explicit POM financial reporting protocols.
risks.evidence: efficiency constraints arising from reliance on legacy information systems requiring manual consolidation

risks.description: Substantial Environmental and Social (E&S) risks associated with financial intermediary sub-loan portfolios.
risks.mitigation: Apply NAFIN's ESMS and PFI due diligence, enforce a ring-fenced Exclusion List, and conduct periodic World Bank sample audits of sub-projects.
risks.evidence: Environmental and Social Risk Classification Substantial

risks.description: High industrial fossil fuel dependence and energy intensity exposing target enterprises to transition risks and energy price spikes.
risks.mitigation: Target sub-loan allocations to energy efficiency, renewable energy scale-up, and decarbonization investments aligned with Mexico's Sustainable Taxonomy.
risks.evidence: This combination of fossil fuels and energy intensity means that firms are exposed to both energy-transition risks and high energy costs.

risks.description: Implementation friction and delay due to novel market application of Sustainability-Linked Loans in the Mexican financial system.
risks.mitigation: Upgrade NAFIN's Sustainable Finance Framework, pilot SLLs in first-tier operations before scaling to second-tier PFIs, and provide extensive capacity building.
risks.evidence: While the Project represents the first systematic application of Sustainability Linked Loan (SLL) and Green Loan (GL) debt instruments in Mexico's financial system
